The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis  
Details:  
The issue described is that JXPath returns null for the XPath expression "//root/@id/text()" when querying an XML document with a root element having an id attribute. This indicates that the descendant-or-self axis is not working correctly from the root node. 

The returned null suggests the context is not correctly traversing descendant nodes starting from the root document node.

Inspection of the `DOMNodePointer.getPointerByID` method shows that it properly fetches the document element by ID using the DOM's `Document.getElementById` method, which is a direct way to get elements by attribute ID, but this path is not used for XPath descendant or self axis traversal. This method handles ID lookups correctly and would return a non-null pointer if the ID is known to the DOM.

The logic that resolves XPath axes and child or descendant nodes likely occurs earlier in pointer navigation or in the compiled expression evaluation, not directly within `getPointerByID`.

The presence of the root element and its ID attribute means that the root node should be included in the descendant or self axes, but the logic is failing to include or find descendants correctly starting from the root.

The test failure at `assertXPathNodeType(context, "//vendor", Element.class);` in the test `testGetNode()` indicates a similar problem: querying with "//vendor" is expected to return the element with that tag anywhere in the document, but it is not.

In summary, the diagnosis based on the bug report and inspected code indicates a bug in the axis traversal logic (descendant-or-self axis) from the root node. The root node or document element is not being included as an accessible starting point for descendant axis resolution, leading to failed lookups such as "//root/@id/text()" returning null.

The ID-based retrieval method is implemented correctly and returns pointers when elements exist, so the problem lies earlier in the XPath descendant traversal mechanism at the root of the document, which fails to discover or return the root and its descendants correctly.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
